column3: “Worthless” renders poor or destitute; the wish to serve the elements becomes a separate question.
The Greek describes his having toiled for them; BSB nominalizes this as his efforts.
The exhortation is moved to the beginning.
The test in his flesh is expanded as his illness being a trial to them; “me” makes explicit the object of despising and rejecting.
“Has become of” supplies a verb; the critical text asks “where” (Ποῦ) your blessedness is, the Textus Receptus “what was” (ἦν) it.
Being zealously sought is rendered as being zealous for a noble purpose.
Hearing the law is expanded as understanding what the law says.
“His son” supplies the referent of the one born from each woman.
“The women represent” makes the allegorical identification explicit.
“Never” makes the negation of travailing more explicit.
“The son” supplies the referent of the one born.
